data.name: Murugesh
data.gender_notes: Murugesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Murugesh, also known as Kartikeya, is the Hindu god of war, knowledge, and love. He is the son of Shiva and Parvati. He holds a vel (a powerful weapon) and a peacock as his mount. He is considered the god of fertility and is often worshiped to ensure the safe delivery of babies. The name Murugesh carries the meaning “God of War and Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Murugesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of war and love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Murugesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of War and Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Murugesh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Murugesh is a revered deity in Tamil Nadu, South India. Along with his brother Ganesha, Murugesh is one of the most popular deities in the Hindu pantheon. He is celebrated through various rituals and festivals, particularly during the month of Aadi (July-August) when his birthday is celebrated as Aadi Perukku. It is believed that devotees who sing the Thiru Murugatruppadai holy verses during this period will earn the god's blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: Murugesh is symbolic of infantry bravery, resilience, knowledge, and compassion. He represents the triumph of spiritual over sensual desires. Through his vel (a thunderbolt-tipped spear), Murugesh reminds devotees of the power of an enlightened mind over material impulses. He is often invoked to help overcome obstacles and challenges, fulfill dreams, and bestow spiritual wisdom. Devotion to Murugesh is believed to purify the mind and uplift the soul.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Murugesh is a name revered in Hinduism, symbolizing the youthful, dynamic, and warrior aspect of Lord Shiva, known as Kartikeya or Subramaniam. It embodies vigor, courage, and victory over adversity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The name Murugesh is mentioned in the Tirumurukāṭṭuppaṭṭu, a Tamil poem from the 7th century. The name Murugesh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The poem describes the god Murugan, who is also known as Murugesh.

trends: increasing popularity as a given name in India
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Murugesh remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Krishna Murugesh in Delhi, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Murugesh, which means "God of War and Love". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
